input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT: a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights", so it fails the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up) and there is no convenience exit elsewhere. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We therefore take the preferred position: § 2.1 is replaced with an express no-minimum-commitment statement, and § 7.1 already limits us to the Fees stated in each Order Form (usage-based where so priced) and bars unidentified minimum-use charges, so we pay only for usage or ordered Services.

mappings.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
mappings.quote: Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

proposal.summary: Replace the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment in § 2.1 with an express no-minimum-commitment statement
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced § 2.1 with an express statement that we have no minimum purchase or volume commitment, consistent with Vendor's acknowledgement in § 12.3 and with § 7.1 (we pay only Order Form Fees and no unidentified minimum-use charges). If a commitment is essential, we could discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
